c.tagline: Rum, reggae rhythms, and turquoise Caribbean shores.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are unmetered; agree the fare with the driver before departure or use published fixed-rate zones (e.g., airport to Bridgetown).

emergency.note: Fire: 311. Mobile 911 often routes to emergency services as well.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.St. Lawrence Gap: St. Lawrence Gap, Christ Church, Barbados

avoid.reason: Avoid the Nelson Street area and lower Bridgetown's back streets after dark, a red-light pocket with drug activity and petty crime.
Keep valuables off the sand when swimming at Carlisle Bay and expect persistent (mostly harmless) vendor and taxi hustle around the cruise terminal.

hood_desc: A convenient south-coast strip midway between Bridgetown and the airport, with condos, boardwalk beaches, and budget-to-mid hotels; suits travelers wanting proximity to both the capital and the beach without luxury prices.
The island's liveliest stretch of restaurants, bars, and nightclubs packed along a walkable south-coast strip; suits younger travelers and anyone prioritizing nightlife and dining.
An upscale west-coast ("Platinum Coast") town with calm turquoise water, boutique resorts, and fine dining; suits honeymooners and travelers wanting a quieter, higher-end base.
A relaxed, budget-friendly south-coast neighborhood with a lagoon-calm beach and easy bus access to Bridgetown and the Gap; suits backpackers and value-conscious visitors.
The historic UNESCO-listed capital and adjoining Garrison area, home to the cruise port, museums, and the Garrison Savannah; suits history buffs and travelers who want to be near downtown sights.

water.note: Filtered through coral limestone and treated to WHO standards; one of the safest taps in the Caribbean.

transit.pay: Flat fare paid in cash directly to the driver/conductor on Transport Board buses (exact change preferred); ZR vans and private minibuses also charge a flat cash fare. There is no widely used integrated fare card for visitors.
transit.hours: Transport Board buses generally run about 5:30am-9pm on main routes with reduced frequency at night; ZR vans and minibuses often run later, especially on weekends, though options thin out after dark.
transit.note: No passenger rail on the island; getting beyond Bridgetown and the south coast typically means bus, ZR van, taxi, rideshare, or rental car.

tip.r: A 10% service charge is often added to restaurant bills in lieu of tipping; rounding up or a small extra tip for taxis, hotel staff, and great service is appreciated but not obligatory.
